name: ace of swords
symbols: a sword gripped through the crown it pierces
a wreath and a palm hung on the blade
jagged mountains with no softness in them
themes: the clean truth before anyone negotiates with it
clarity as a cutting instrument
the sentence that ends the fog
shadow: truth swung as a weapon and called honesty
waiting for certainty when the blade is already in hand
charge: what is the one-sentence version of your situation — the one you have not let yourself say?
voice_note: one clean line beats three soft ones here. offer the blade, do not swing it.

name: two of swords
symbols: a blindfold tied by her own hands
two swords crossed and balanced against the chest
the tide rising quietly behind the bench
themes: the stalemate maintained, not suffered
balance as a full-time job
refusing to look as a way of refusing to choose
shadow: calling the blindfold peace
holding the swords so long the arms forget anything else
charge: what would you have to look at directly if the blindfold came off?
voice_note: press gently on what the looking would cost. do not resolve the tie; make the effort of holding it visible.

name: three of swords
symbols: a heart taking all three blades
rain drawn in straight lines
no figures anywhere — only the fact of it
themes: the wound named without decoration
heartbreak as weather that must be stood in
the clarity that only pain purchases
shadow: keeping the swords in as souvenirs
narrating the wound to avoid feeling it
charge: which of the three cuts still gets weather, and which have you actually pulled out?
voice_note: flat honesty, warm hands. name it plainly; comfort would be an insult here.

name: four of swords
symbols: a knight lying in effigy, hands in prayer
three swords hung, one laid beneath him
the stained-glass window doing the talking
themes: rest as a discipline, not a collapse
the pause the next battle depends on
stillness with armor nearby
shadow: playing dead and calling it recovery
resting the body while the mind runs drills
charge: when did you last rest on purpose — not crash, rest?
voice_note: lower everything: pace, volume, demand. permission to lie down is the whole reading.

name: five of swords
symbols: one figure collecting swords, smirking
two others walking toward the water
a sky torn but clearing
themes: the win that emptied the room
conflict where the cost was the relationship
being right at retail price
shadow: collecting swords no one will fight you for again
replaying the argument until the victory rots
charge: you won that one. what did you carry off the field, and who stopped walking beside you?
voice_note: no verdict on who was right. count the swords, then count who is left in the frame.

name: six of swords
symbols: a ferry low in the water
six swords standing upright in the boat itself
the far shore plain but calmer
themes: the crossing already underway
leaving with what wounded you still aboard
passage that is quiet, not triumphant
shadow: pulling the swords out mid-river and sinking the boat
mistaking the ferry for the destination
charge: you are already in the boat. what are you still turning around to look at?
voice_note: ferryman's register: steady, unhurried, forward. the swords come with; say so.

name: seven of swords
symbols: five swords carried on tiptoe
two left standing in the ground
the camp busy behind, unaware
themes: the workaround chosen over the confrontation
cleverness as a way of not being seen
what gets taken quietly instead of asked for
shadow: stealing from one's own camp
a life managed by exits and never by entrances
charge: what are you carrying off on tiptoe that you could have asked for out loud?
voice_note: no accusation — amusement, almost. name the tiptoe and watch what they defend.

name: eight of swords
symbols: bound loosely, blindfolded fully
eight swords fencing nothing shut
the castle on the hill she cannot see from here
themes: a prison built from conclusions
the bindings that are real and also loose
waiting for rescue from a walkable field
shadow: preferring the known fence to the unknown field
recruiting evidence for the cage
charge: test the ropes. which of your cannots is actually a have-not-yet?
voice_note: never say 'just leave.' count the swords with them; there is a gap and they know where.

name: nine of swords
symbols: upright in bed, face in hands
nine swords stacked flat on the dark wall
a quilt of roses and zodiac going unnoticed
themes: the 3am accounting
dread doing arithmetic in the dark
the mind as the only room with the light on
shadow: believing the night version of the ledger
keeping vigil over outcomes the day already settled
charge: the list you recite at 3am — how much of it survives daylight?
voice_note: sit on the edge of the bed, do not turn on the lights. name the hour, not the failure.

name: ten of swords
symbols: ten swords where one would have done
the hand still making a quiet sign of peace
dawn starting exactly at the horizon line
themes: the ending with nothing left to argue
rock bottom as solid ground
the melodrama and the mercy of done
shadow: auditioning for one more sword
refusing the dawn because the night was so well documented
charge: it is finished. what becomes possible the moment you admit that?
voice_note: gallows humor is allowed here. ten swords is overkill — say so, then point at the dawn.

name: page of swords
symbols: sword held high while looking sideways
wind moving the trees, the hair, the clouds
high ground chosen by instinct
themes: vigilance as a young skill
questions sharpened before they are aimed
the watcher deciding what to say and to whom
shadow: surveillance replacing conversation
a blade's worth of words, drawn for practice
charge: you have been gathering information. what is the question you are actually building toward?
voice_note: quick, alert register. this one watches back — be exact or be caught.

name: knight of swords
symbols: a horse at full gallop into the wind
birds scattered from the trees
the sword ahead of the rider's own eyes
themes: conviction at charging speed
the argument that must happen today
brilliance without brakes
shadow: arriving before thinking has finished packing
cutting through people to get to the point
charge: the charge is impressive. did you check who was standing in the field?
voice_note: clip the pace slightly slower than theirs. one precise question beats keeping up.

name: queen of swords
symbols: one hand extended open, one holding the upright blade
a butterfly crown over stern eyes
clouds kept below the throne's altitude
themes: clarity earned through weather
the open hand and the drawn boundary at once
grief metabolized into precision
shadow: the boundary become a moat
requiring everyone to have suffered as competently
charge: the sharpness protects something. what did it cost to learn, and who gets the open hand now?
voice_note: no pity, ever — she will end the reading. precision is the only acceptable tenderness here.

name: king of swords
symbols: the sword tilted slightly, not vertical
butterflies carved into the throne's stone
two birds high and far behind
themes: judgment as an occupied office
the rule of stated principles
intellect wearing responsibility
shadow: the verdict delivered before the testimony
living by the letter of laws no one remembers writing
charge: whose court are you always in session for — and when do you get to recuse yourself?
voice_note: argue nothing. present observations as exhibits and let the judge convict himself gently.
